rationale:
**Violated for some non-ASCII names; holds for every ASCII name.**

How it is implemented: `cargo agents search <query>` reaches `search_command::search`, which calls `find_matches` and reports every match it returns, grouped by origin (one `SearchMatch` event per hit, or a single nothing-found notice). In `find_matches` the first arm loads `plugins::load_registry` (`load_registry_impl` with no workspace): it iterates every *trusted* PM instance, i.e. every configured registry (the builtin `symposium-recommendations`, `user-plugins`, and each `[[registry]]` entry), and takes all of `registry_plugins()`. Nothing there filters by `[plugins] disable`, dormancy, or dependency predicates; a dormant plugin is still listed, with a dormant hint as its description. Every plugin whose `manifest.name` passes `name_matches` is pushed unconditionally. The package-manager arm that follows only adds or skips hits, so it cannot remove a registry-plugin match. A registry that cannot be read (for example a git registry that was never fetched, even after the binary's `ensure_registries`) contributes no plugins. In that case no plugin is known to the command at all, which the code reports as a warning.

Matching: `name_matches` is `name.to_lowercase().contains(&query.to_lowercase())`. That is case-insensitive for ASCII and for most Unicode text. It is not full case folding, though, and lowercasing each string separately depends on context. Rust maps a capital sigma `Σ` to final `ς` at the end of a word and to `σ` elsewhere. So for a plugin named `ΟΔΟΣΑ` (lowercased `οδοσα`), the query `ΟΔΟΣ` lowercases to `οδος` and does **not** match, even though the name contains the query byte for byte. I confirmed this with a standalone `rustc` probe of the same expression. Plugin `name` values are not restricted to ASCII: `validate_manifest` only requires a name for registry manifests, and a bare skill's name comes from its frontmatter. So a configured-registry plugin whose name contains `<query>` can go unlisted. Strings whose case mapping is not one-to-one, such as `ß` vs `SS`, are also not treated as equal.

Tests (both pass; `cargo test -q --test enablement search_`): `search_finds_registry_content_tagged_by_origin` asserts the case-insensitive substring match on the `plugins0` fixture (`SERDE-gui` finds `serde-guidance`; `my-skill` and `MY-SKILL` find `my-skill` with origin `user-plugins`) and that a query with no matches returns empty. `search_renders_grouped_by_origin` asserts the rendered report carries a `search_match` for `serde-guidance` under `user-plugins` and only a nothing-found notice when nothing matches. Both use ASCII names from a single registry. `search_lists_a_registry_entry_once` (tests/enablement.rs:455, passes, not cited for this requirement and not an input here) also requires that the matching registry plugin is listed, including plugin `foo` in entry dir `foo-tools`. Multiple registries, dormant plugins, and non-ASCII names are untested and judged from the code.

To hold as written, matching would need a context-free comparison such as Unicode case folding, or ASCII-only plugin names enforced at validation. Alternatively, the requirement could scope itself to ASCII case.
requirement: `cargo agents search <query>` MUST list every configured-registry plugin whose name contains `<query>`, ignoring case.
